objectives: Describe the magnetic field of a current-carrying wire and solenoid and use of electromagnets.
Describe the motor effect and Fleming's left-hand rule.
Describe electromagnetic induction and use the transformer equation.

blocks.title: Magnetic effect of a current
blocks.md: A **current in a wire produces a magnetic field** in circles around the wire (right-hand grip rule: thumb along the current, fingers show the field). A **coil (solenoid)** gives a field like a bar magnet. An **electromagnet** has a soft-iron core in a coil: it is stronger with **more turns**, a **larger current** and an **iron core**, and it can be switched off. Uses: cranes lifting scrap iron, electric bells, relays, loudspeakers.

items.text: magnetic field from N to S

blocks.caption: A wire carrying a current across a magnetic field feels a force (here upwards).
blocks.alt: A magnet with N on the left and S on the right, field arrows pointing to the right, and a wire with current out of the page with a green force arrow pointing up.

blocks.title: The motor effect
blocks.md: A **current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a force**, at right angles to both. **Fleming's left-hand rule**: **first finger = Field** (N to S), **seCond finger = Current**, **thuMb = Motion** (force). The force is larger for a bigger current, a stronger field or a longer wire. A **d.c. motor** has a coil in a field, a **commutator** that reverses the current every half turn and **brushes**, so the coil keeps turning.

blocks.title: Electromagnetic induction
blocks.md: A **voltage (e.m.f.) is induced** when a magnet moves into or out of a coil, or when a wire cuts magnetic field lines: it is larger for a **faster** movement, a **stronger** magnet and **more turns**. No movement gives no e.m.f. A **generator (dynamo)** turns a coil in a field and gives **alternating current**. A **transformer** has two coils on an iron core: **Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np**. A **step-up** transformer has Ns > Np; **step-down** Ns < Np. Transformers only work with **a.c.**

blocks.caption: A transformer: two coils on a laminated iron core.
blocks.alt: A rectangular iron core with a primary coil of Np turns on the left limb and a secondary coil of Ns turns on the right limb.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A transformer does not work on d.c.: a changing field is needed.
- It cannot increase power: for an ideal transformer Vp Ip = Vs Is, so a higher voltage means a lower current.
- The thumb in Fleming's left-hand rule shows the **force**, not the current.

blocks.title: Step-down transformer
blocks.statement: A transformer has 500 turns on the primary and 50 turns on the secondary. The primary is connected to 220 V a.c. Find the secondary voltage.
steps: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np, so Vs = 220 × 50 ÷ 500.

blocks.title: Current in the primary
blocks.statement: The secondary of that ideal transformer supplies 2 A at 22 V. Find the current in the primary.
steps: Power out = 22 × 2 = 44 W; ideal: power in = 44 W.
